topic: pagination of a public REST API
old_rule: Every list endpoint is paginated by page number, the client sending page_number from 1 and page_size up to 100, and every response carries an X-Total-Count header with the size of the whole filtered collection.
new_rule: Every list endpoint is paginated by an opaque cursor, the client sending limit up to 200 and the cursor from the previous response's next_cursor field, and a response without next_cursor is the last one.

planted.text: Responses carry no X-Total-Count header, so progress bars have to be sized some other way.
A client no longer works out where the next request starts from the number of the page it is on and the size of each page.
Jumping straight to an arbitrary point in the middle of a collection is not something clients can do any more.
The sort key is chosen from the list the endpoint publishes, not composed by the client as a free-form expression.
An unreadable cursor is reported as an error, never silently taken as a request for the first items.
Our cursors carry no such promise, and their contents may change in any release without notice.
planted.licence: Some public APIs document their cursor format so that clients can build cursors of their own.

planted.text: That pattern fails against this API, since a cursor lapses fifteen minutes after it was issued.
planted.licence: Several popular client libraries store the next link and follow it hours later.

planted.text: The API cannot serve that request yet, and no response carries a cursor for the preceding items.
planted.licence: The mobile team has asked the SDKs to let a feed scroll backwards.

planted.text: A request that omits the limit parameter receives fifty items by default.
The server never returns more items than the limit the response reports.
